question: When you pull a corner to round it, should it round every corner or just that one?
context: Two features built a month apart chose opposite defaults. Audit: queue/audits/2026-10-04-round-a-path-s-corners.json (its second evaluate question asks this).

options.label: Every corner on a plain pull, Option for one; rectangles change to match
options.summary: Pulling any corner handle rounds all the corners together, on a rectangle and on a shape you drew. Hold Option to round only the corner you are pulling. This is how drawn shapes already work, and rectangles switch over.
pros: Same as Photoshop, Figma and Illustrator
Drawn shapes already work this way, so only rectangles change
The common case, all corners alike, takes no key
cons: Anyone used to the rectangle's one corner pull has to add Option for it
options.mitigation: The pill under the shape names what is changing as you pull, so the first pull shows which way it went.

options.label: Just that corner on a plain pull, Option for all; drawn shapes change to match
options.summary: Pulling a corner handle rounds only that corner, on a rectangle and on a shape you drew. Hold Option to round them all. This is how rectangles already work, and drawn shapes switch over.
pros: Rectangles keep working the way they do today
Rounding one corner, the finer job, takes no key
cons: The reverse of Photoshop, Figma and Illustrator
Rounding a whole shape takes Option every time
options.mitigation: The Corner Radius slider in Appearance still rounds every corner in one move.

options.label: Leave them different
options.summary: Rectangles keep rounding one corner on a plain pull and drawn shapes keep rounding every corner. Nothing changes.
pros: No work, and nothing anyone has learned changes
cons: Learning one teaches you the other backwards
